name: Georgia

governingStatutes.name: Georgia Rules of the State Board of Workers' Compensation

covered: All employees if employer elects coverage

benefitCategories.medical: All authorized treatment; employer/insurer selects Authorized Treating Physician (ATP) from panel
benefitCategories.temporaryTotal: 66 2/3% of wages up to max ($750/week—one of lowest in nation); max 400 weeks
benefitCategories.temporaryPartial: 66 2/3% of wage difference up to $416/week; max 350 weeks
benefitCategories.permanentPartial: Schedule (specific loss) by weeks per body part × 66 2/3% of wages; non-schedule by residual earning capacity
benefitCategories.permanentTotal: 66 2/3% of wages up to max; 400 weeks (catastrophic: lifetime with higher cap)
benefitCategories.catastrophic: Defined injuries (e.g., amputation, paralysis, severe TBI); higher weekly max; lifetime duration
benefitCategories.deathBenefits: 66 2/3% of wages to dependents; max 400 weeks; $7,500 burial

workersCompensation.initialClaimForm: WC-14 (Notice of Claim/First Report) by employer; Form WC-14a if employee initiates

appealLevels.name: Administrative Law Judge (ALJ)
appealLevels.deadline: 1 year from injury or last payment

workersCompensation.enforcementPowers: SBWC compliance investigations; penalty assessment; fraud unit
workersCompensation.penalties: 15% penalty for late payment (plus interest); 20% for unreasonable denial; uninsured employer penalties

programs.name: No State Disability Insurance
programs.note: Georgia has no state temporary disability insurance program

programs.name: Georgia Medicaid
programs.eligibility: Low-income; Georgia has not expanded Medicaid under ACA

programs.name: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families
programs.administeringBody: GA Division of Family & Children Services
programs.eligibility: Very low income families with children; strict limits

constitutionalProtections.source: Georgia Constitution Art. I, § 1, Para. II
Georgia Constitution Art. I, § 1, Para. I

statutes.name: Georgia Equal Employment for People with Disabilities Code
statutes.protections: Disability discrimination in employment; follows ADA framework

statutes.name: Georgia Whistleblower Protection
statutes.protections: Protection for public employees reporting fraud/abuse

protectedClasses: Note: Georgia has no comprehensive state civil rights law covering race, sex, religion in private employment—rely on federal law
civilRightsFramework.federalReliance: Georgia relies heavily on federal civil rights law (Title VII, ADA, ADEA) for private employment; limited state protections
civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Limited to disability discrimination and public employee whistleblower contexts; federal law provides broader coverage

accommodationObligations.standard: Reasonable accommodation per federal ADA and Georgia disability code

enablingStatutes.disability: No state TDI; O.C.G.A. Title 49 (public assistance)
enablingStatutes.civilRights: O.C.G.A. § 34-6A (disability only); no comprehensive state civil rights act

delegatedBodies.authority: Limited discrimination complaints; no enforcement power for private employment

laborStandards.authority: Limited labor law enforcement; primarily unemployment administration

civilRights.authority: Limited scope; primarily handles housing discrimination; refers employment to EEOC
civilRights.deadline: 180 days (EEOC deadline applies for federal claims)

occupationalSafety.authority: Georgia is not a state plan state; OSHA covers private sector; no state OSHA

complianceMechanisms: EEOC primary venue for employment discrimination

filingDeadlines.wcClaim: 1 year from injury or last voluntary payment
filingDeadlines.eeocCharge: 180 days (or 300 with state agency worksharing—limited in GA)

evidentiaryStandards.wc: Preponderance of evidence; ATP opinion significant
evidentiaryStandards.appeal: Any evidence standard on Superior Court review

judicialReview.wc: ALJ → SBWC Appellate Division → Superior Court → Court of Appeals → Supreme Court
judicialReview.civilRights: EEOC → Federal court (or state court for state disability code)
judicialReview.note: Federal enforcement primary for most discrimination claims

specialConsiderations.lowBenefits: Georgia has one of the lowest maximum weekly WC benefits ($750/week) in the nation; inadequate wage replacement for higher earners
specialConsiderations.noComprehensiveCivilRightsLaw: Georgia is one of few states without a comprehensive state civil rights law covering private employment discrimination beyond disability; workers must rely on federal law
specialConsiderations.atpControl: Employer/insurer controls Authorized Treating Physician selection; limits worker choice
specialConsiderations.catastrophicDesignation: Catastrophic injury designation critical—provides lifetime benefits and higher weekly max; worth fighting for qualifying injuries
